shorts.title: Why the Strait of Hormuz Matters
shorts.covers: About a fifth of the world's oil passes through a strait between Iran and Oman that is about 21 miles wide at its narrowest.
shorts.source: US Energy Information Administration and reporting from multiple outlets

shorts.title: NATO's Article 5, Explained
shorts.covers: What 'an attack on one is an attack on all' really commits members to, and the only time it has been used, after 9/11.
shorts.source: The North Atlantic Treaty text and NATO's own history

shorts.title: Why Taiwan Matters to Everyone
shorts.covers: One island makes most of the world's most advanced chips, and Beijing and Taipei disagree about what Taiwan is.
shorts.source: TSMC and industry data, and official positions of Beijing, Taipei and Washington

shorts.title: Kashmir in Three Minutes
shorts.covers: How the partition of 1947 left Kashmir divided and claimed by both India and Pakistan, and why it keeps flaring up.
shorts.source: UN resolutions, the Simla Agreement, and Indian and Pakistani official positions

shorts.title: The South China Sea Line
shorts.covers: China's nine-dash line claim, the 2016 tribunal ruling China rejects, and why the Philippines, Vietnam and others care.
shorts.source: The 2016 Permanent Court of Arbitration award and official statements

shorts.title: How the UN Security Council Veto Works
shorts.covers: Five countries can block any Security Council decision, and why that was designed in 1945.
shorts.source: The UN Charter and UN records of vetoes

shorts.title: Why Crimea Matters So Much
shorts.covers: A peninsula with a warm-water naval base at Sevastopol, transferred inside the USSR in 1954 and annexed by Russia in 2014.
shorts.source: Standard histories and UN General Assembly Resolution 68/262

shorts.title: The Suez Canal and the World's Shopping
shorts.covers: About an eighth of world trade passes through one Egyptian canal, and a single stuck ship in 2021 showed why.
shorts.source: Suez Canal Authority figures and reporting on the Ever Given

shorts.title: Nord Stream: Gas, Pipes and Power
shorts.covers: How Europe came to depend on Russian gas, and what happened to the Nord Stream pipelines in September 2022.
shorts.source: European energy data and reporting on the pipeline investigations

shorts.title: The Abraham Accords
shorts.covers: In 2020 Israel normalised relations with the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan, and what it meant for the Palestinian question.
shorts.source: The accords texts and official statements of all parties

shorts.title: What Is BRICS For?
shorts.covers: Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa formed a club that is now growing, and what its members want from it.
shorts.source: BRICS summit declarations and reporting

shorts.title: The Panama Canal and Who Controls It
shorts.covers: The US built it, handed it to Panama in 1999, and a drought and a political fight have put it back in the news.
shorts.source: Panama Canal Authority and the Torrijos-Carter Treaties

shorts.title: The Korean DMZ
shorts.covers: A strip of land 4 kilometres wide has divided Korea since the 1953 armistice; the war never officially ended.
shorts.source: The Korean Armistice Agreement and standard histories

shorts.title: Why Greenland Matters
shorts.covers: The world's largest island belongs to Denmark, sits between America and Europe, and holds rare minerals under its ice.
shorts.source: Danish and Greenlandic government positions and US statements

shorts.title: The Indus Waters Treaty
shorts.covers: In 1960 India and Pakistan agreed how to share six rivers, and India suspended the treaty in April 2025.
shorts.source: The treaty text, World Bank records and official statements

shorts.title: The Houthis and the Red Sea
shorts.covers: A Yemeni armed movement began attacking ships in the Red Sea in late 2023 and changed the routes of world shipping.
shorts.source: UN reports, shipping data and reporting from multiple outlets

shorts.title: Who Are the Kurds?
shorts.covers: About thirty million people across Turkey, Iraq, Syria and Iran, often called the largest nation without a state.
shorts.source: Standard histories and official positions of the governments involved

shorts.title: Sudan's Forgotten War
shorts.covers: Since April 2023 two Sudanese generals have fought for control of the country, causing one of the world's largest displacement crises.
shorts.source: UN OCHA and UNHCR reports and reporting from multiple outlets

shorts.title: The Coup Belt of the Sahel
shorts.covers: Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger had military coups between 2020 and 2023, turned away from France, and toward Russia.
shorts.source: ECOWAS statements and reporting from multiple outlets

shorts.title: Why Oil Is Sold in Dollars
shorts.covers: The 1970s deal that made the US dollar the currency of oil, and why that gives America unusual power.
shorts.source: Economic histories of the petrodollar and IMF data

shorts.title: The Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
shorts.covers: In 1968 most countries agreed not to build nuclear weapons; four of the nine that have them never signed or left.
shorts.source: The NPT text and IAEA records

shorts.title: The Chagos Islands Deal
shorts.covers: Britain removed the islanders in the 1960s to make way for a US base, and agreed in 2025 to hand sovereignty to Mauritius.
shorts.source: The ICJ 2019 advisory opinion and UK and Mauritian government statements

shorts.title: Kaliningrad: Russia Inside the EU
shorts.covers: A piece of Russia between Poland and Lithuania, cut off from the rest of the country and heavily armed.
shorts.source: Standard histories and official statements

shorts.title: Transnistria: A Country That Isn't
shorts.covers: A breakaway strip of Moldova with its own currency and army that almost no country recognises.
shorts.source: OSCE reports and official positions

shorts.title: Kosovo's Unfinished Independence
shorts.covers: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008; about half the world recognises it and Serbia does not.
shorts.source: The ICJ 2010 advisory opinion and official positions

shorts.title: Nagorno-Karabakh: The End of a Republic
shorts.covers: In September 2023 Azerbaijan took control of the enclave, and almost all its Armenian population left within days.
shorts.source: UNHCR figures and official statements from both sides

shorts.title: Venezuela and the Essequibo
shorts.covers: Venezuela claims two-thirds of neighbouring Guyana, where huge oil fields were found offshore.
shorts.source: ICJ case documents and official statements

shorts.title: Rare Earths: The Minerals Behind Everything
shorts.covers: Phones, wind turbines and fighter jets need rare earth metals, and most are processed in China.
shorts.source: US Geological Survey and IEA data

shorts.title: The Malacca Strait
shorts.covers: The shortest sea route between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific runs past Singapore, and China calls its dependence on it a dilemma.
shorts.source: Shipping data and official statements

shorts.title: Hong Kong: One Country, Two Systems
shorts.covers: Britain handed Hong Kong to China in 1997 with a promise of fifty years of separate freedoms, and what changed in 2020.
shorts.source: The Sino-British Joint Declaration, the 2020 National Security Law, and official statements
